run.question: Database connection timeouts are occurring for blue-whale app in namespace app-94

report.summary: Investigated the reported database connection timeouts for the blue-whale app in namespace app-94 using the runbook database-troubleshooting (skill_id database-troubleshooting, revision 1). What the cluster shows: the only workload in app-94 is Deployment blue-whale (1/1 ready), whose single pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-crnfq is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and was started at 2026-11-23T16:33:50Z; its container env is DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20, and its application code is mounted from a Secret whose contents are not readable. The database Service it points at, Service app-94/postgres (ClusterIP 10.96.37.91, 5432->5432, selector app=postgres-db), has an Endpoints object with subsets: null, i.e. no addresses or ports, while the blue-whale Endpoints does list the blue-whale pod. A cluster-wide listing found no postgres Deployment, Pod or StatefulSet in any namespace (25 Deployments, 33 Pods, 1 StatefulSet = alertmanager/otel-demo), so the selector app=postgres-db matches nothing. No NetworkPolicy exists in app-94 and no ResourceQuota exists anywhere, so neither is blocking traffic or scheduling. The 6 events retained in the window are all Normal and all in app-94 at 16:33:49-16:33:50Z (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet 0->1, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started); there is no Evicted, OOMKilled, Failed or Unhealthy event. The blue-whale pod was therefore created during the window by its own Deployment controller, which is a rollout/scale-up mechanism, not damage, and is not counted as impact. The strongest supported cause is that the database Service has no backing endpoints because no postgres workload exists - a fact about the Service and endpoints, matching runbook step 3 ('No Database Endpoints'). However the reported symptom itself (timeout errors) is not directly observed anywhere: the blue-whale container's current log stream returned 0 bytes and has no previous instance, and Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for every query in this Run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so there is no error-rate, latency baseline or trace evidence for blue-whale or postgres. The conclusion is therefore partial: an endpoint-less database Service is evidenced; the timeout text, its exact error form (refused vs timeout), when the DB backend disappeared, and any downstream/customer impact remain unverified. Runbook steps carried out: (1) application status - checked (pod Running/Ready/0 restarts, only Normal creation events); (2) application logs - attempted, 0 lines / no previous container, no timeout text observed; (3) database service and endpoints - checked (Service exists, Endpoints empty, no DB workload); (4) connectivity test from the pod to the DB (nc/kubectl exec) - could not be carried out, no exec capability among the available tools; (5) database health query (psql SELECT 1, pg_stat_activity) - not possible, no database pod exists to exec into; (6) connection pool configuration - checked via the Deployment env (DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20).

claims.text: Deployment app-94/blue-whale runs 1 replica with 1 ready/available, image python:3.9-slim, command python /app/app.py, env DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20, and mounts its application code from a Secret volume (contents not readable).
Service app-94/postgres exists as ClusterIP 10.96.37.91 with port 5432 -> targetPort 5432 and selector app=postgres-db, which is the address configured in blue-whale's DB_HOST/DB_PORT.

Endpoints app-94/postgres has subsets: null (no addresses, no ports), whereas Endpoints app-94/blue-whale lists address 10.244.0.38 port 8080 targeting pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-crnfq; the database Service therefore has no backing endpoint.

A cluster-wide listing found no postgres database workload: of 25 Deployments (no truncation reported) none is postgres and none runs a postgres image, of 33 Pods none carries label app=postgres-db or a postgres name, and the only StatefulSet is alertmanager in otel-demo; the only pod in app-94 is blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-crnfq, so Service postgres's selector app=postgres-db matches no object.

The blue-whale pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-crnfq is Running and Ready (conditions Initialized/Ready/ContainersReady/PodScheduled all True), restartCount 0, container state running since 2026-11-23T16:33:50Z, owned by ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5, which is owned by Deployment blue-whale.

The 6 events retained inside the authorized window are all Normal and all in app-94 between 2026-11-23T16:33:49Z and 16:33:50Z: Deployment blue-whale ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 from 0 to 1', ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 SuccessfulCreate 'Created pod: blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-crnfq', and Pod Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started; there is no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, Failed or Unhealthy event.

No NetworkPolicy objects exist in app-94 (the query returned zero objects) and no ResourceQuota objects exist in any namespace, so neither a network policy nor a quota is preventing pod-to-pod traffic or database scheduling at query time.
Cluster DNS is present and fully available: Deployment kube-system/coredns has replicas 2, ready 2, available 2.

The most likely cause of the reported timeouts is that blue-whale connects to postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432 but Service app-94/postgres has no endpoints and no postgres workload exists in the cluster, so every database connection attempt has no destination and fails/times out. This is supported by the configuration and endpoint facts but not by any observed application error text, trace or metric.

A second candidate that cannot be excluded without metrics or logs is connection-pool exhaustion or an over-aggressive connect timeout inside blue-whale (DB_POOL_SIZE=20, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30): the deployment env values are visible, but the application code inside the Secret volume and any pool metrics/errors are not observable in this Run.

A third candidate is name resolution for postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local failing at runtime; the coredns Deployment is fully ready, but no DNS query evidence (e.g. coredns log lines) was obtained, so DNS behaviour during the timeouts is untested rather than ruled out.

Rejected: a crash/restart, OOMKilled or eviction of the blue-whale pod as the source of the failures. The pod has restartCount 0, no previous container instance, all Ready conditions True, and the only events are Normal creation events from its own Deployment/ReplicaSet (Scaled up 0 to 1, SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started) with no Evicted, OOMKilled or Unhealthy event.

The blue-whale pod's creation during the window is a scale-up by its own controller (Deployment blue-whale Scaled up ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 from 0 to 1 at 2026-11-23T16:33:49Z), not an externally applied fault; nothing in the retained evidence names an object injecting a fault into app-94.

Restore the missing database backend: create/apply the postgres workload in app-94 with label app=postgres-db (or correct Service postgres's selector to the labels its existing database pods actually carry), then confirm Endpoints app-94/postgres gains addresses/ports and retest connections from blue-whale.

Once telemetry is reachable, check blue-whale's own error/log signals and postgres connection counts (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity) to separate a missing-backend failure from pool exhaustion, and make the application log connection errors to stdout so future occurrences are directly observable.

gaps: Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for every query in this Run: execute_prometheus_instant_query('up'), traces_list_services, get_metric_names and get_all_labels each returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. No metric, error-rate, latency baseline or trace evidence for blue-whale or postgres could be obtained, so the reported timeouts are supported only by configuration and Kubernetes object state.

No application error text was observed: fetch_pod_logs for blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-crnfq returned 0 bytes / 0 lines (status no_data) for the current container and reported no previous container instance; a filtered query for timeout|connect|error|postgres|database also returned nothing. A similarly empty coredns log read produced no DNS evidence.

The blue-whale application code is mounted from a Secret volume (name redacted in the deployment annotation) and secrets cannot be read, so the actual connection logic, retry and pooling behaviour could not be verified.

The runbook's connectivity test from the blue-whale pod to the database (nc/kubectl exec) and its database health check (psql SELECT 1, pg_stat_activity) could not be carried out: no exec tool is available and no database pod exists to exec into.

It is unknown when the postgres backend disappeared, whether one ever existed in app-94, and who changed it: only 6 events were retained (all Normal creation events at 2026-11-23T16:33:49-16:33:50Z) and the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
Impact is not widened by inference: no evidence was observed of failures in any caller of blue-whale, and no downstream or customer impact was verified.
Whether blue-whale itself is returning errors to its own callers cannot be confirmed: its Service has the pod as an endpoint, but no request metrics or traces exist for it in this Run.
next_steps: Apply the postgres database workload (or fix Service postgres's selector) in namespace app-94 so Endpoints app-94/postgres has addresses on port 5432, then re-check Endpoints and test connectivity from blue-whale.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger reachability and re-query blue-whale error spans/metrics and postgres connection counts to confirm the failure mode (connection refused/timeout versus pool exhaustion).
Collect the blue-whale container's stdout/stderr after the next failure window, since the current stream is empty and provides no diagnostic text.
If the database is externally managed or lives in another namespace, verify DB_HOST postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local against the real database endpoint and update the Deployment env if it is stale.
